events.text: The rice jar above you is low this winter. You can feel it in the weight: a hand's depth of grain where there should be an arm's. Up in the kitchen, the youngest child of the house is told there will be no second bowl.
variants: New rice comes into the jar above you, the first of the harvest. It pours in like warm rain and the whole house laughs. You feel full without eating.
The grandmother of the house sets a bowl of clear water on the jar-lid and bows to it. To you. She does not know where you are, exactly, but she knows you are there.

choices.text: Draw the cold out of the storeroom floor

effects.log: You pull the frost from the ground under the jar into yourself. The grain keeps. The family eats a little longer than the arithmetic says it should.

choices.text: Hold still and keep your warmth for spring

effects.log: You keep it. Spring will need it more than winter does, and you are a small thing yet.

choices.text: Tremble once, so the mother checks the jar

effects.log: She checks it, finds a mouse-hole, and plugs it. A whole sack was going out the back of the jar. Not a famine after all: a mouse.

events.text: The house above you has a quarrel in it: two brothers and an inheritance. The floor is thick with it, like smoke that will not go up the chimney.

choices.text: Make the floor creak at the worst moment

effects.log: Every time one of them raises a voice the floor complains. By the third evening they are laughing at it, and then at themselves.

choices.text: Stay out of human quarrels

effects.log: You sink a little deeper and wait. The quarrel goes on all winter and ends the way quarrels do, tired.

choices.text: Warm the side of the house where the younger one sleeps

effects.log: He sleeps better and wakes kinder. In the spring he gives way about the field, and the house is quiet again.

events.text: Threshing day. The flails come down on your back all morning, hundreds of them, in a rhythm that the whole yard knows. It does not hurt. It is like being drummed.
variants: New Year, and the troupe in masks has come to stamp the yard for luck. Their feet come down on you in a dance a thousand years older than any of them.
Children are playing hopscotch over your head, a grid of nine squares scratched in the dirt. The middle square is right above your heart. Every child who lands there laughs.

choices.text: Drum back, very slightly

effects.log: The flails fall into your rhythm without knowing it. The threshing goes faster than anyone can remember. The headman credits a new song.

choices.text: Soak up the shaking and grow

effects.log: Every stroke goes into you. By evening you are a little longer under the yard, and the chaff above you smells like a feast.

choices.text: Listen to the songs they sing

effects.log: Old songs about harvests, older songs about a dragon under the earth. They have it nearly right.

events.text: The village is digging a new well at the edge of the threshing yard. You can feel the spade strokes coming down toward a seam of bad water, the kind that sickens children.

choices.text: Turn the seam aside under the earth

effects.log: It is slow, heavy work, like rolling a log in your sleep. The diggers hit sweet water the next morning and never know how close it was.

choices.text: Make the ground too hard to dig there

effects.log: The spades ring on stone. The diggers curse and move ten paces east, to sweet water. The headman decides the earth is particular.

choices.text: Let them dig, and see what humans do

effects.log: They hit the bad water, taste it, spit, and fill the hole in. Humans are not as foolish as the stories say.

events.text: The well you guarded has a stone rim now, and the village has carved a little dragon on it, curled round the rim, yellow with clay. A child puts a rice cake on it every morning.

choices.text: Send up a cool breath into the well each summer

effects.log: The well is the coldest in the county. People walk from other villages for its water.

choices.text: Eat the rice cake: it is offered

effects.log: It is the first offering you have ever eaten. It tastes of the child's hands and of new rice. Something in you grows by a span.

choices.text: Leave the cakes for the birds

effects.log: The magpies of the yard grow fat and loud. The child thinks the dragon has a great many beaks.

events.text: Five roads meet over you, and each brings its own weight: carts of salt from the east road, cattle from the south, soldiers from the west. You are learning to tell them apart by the way they press on the earth.
variants: A funeral and a wedding meet at the crossroads above you, coming from two roads at once. Neither will give way. The earth under both of them is you.
A blind fortune-teller sets up a mat over your heart and tells every traveller the truth, which is bad for business. The roads are all she reads.

choices.text: Follow the salt carts with your mind

effects.log: East, and east, and on to the sea. You have never seen the sea. Now, a little, through the carts, you have.

choices.text: Weigh the soldiers

effects.log: Too many, too heavy, too fast. There will be a battle somewhere to the north. You warn nobody, because you cannot speak, and remember it.

choices.text: Make the five roads equal for a day

effects.log: A day when every road is easy. Travellers on all five arrive early and cannot say why. A merchant marries a traveller he met at the crossing.

events.text: Wood, fire, earth, metal, water: the five phases turn through the crossroads as the five roads do, and for the first time you feel yourself as the one in the middle that the others turn around.

choices.text: Sit at the centre and let them turn

effects.log: You do not move. The phases go round you like a wheel round an axle. You understand something about being the axle.

choices.text: Push the wheel, just once

effects.log: It turns a little faster. That year spring comes early on all five roads, and autumn late. You feel very tired.

choices.text: Hold the wheel still for a breath

effects.log: For one breath the world does not turn. Nobody notices. You do.

events.text: A robber has taken to waiting at the crossroads at dusk, where the five roads give him five ways to run. You can feel him standing on you every evening, heavy with stolen silver.

choices.text: Soften the earth under his feet

effects.log: The next time he runs, the road takes his ankle like a hand. The villagers catch him in a ditch.

choices.text: Make all five roads lead back to the crossing

effects.log: He runs five ways in one night and arrives back where he started each time. In the morning he sits down in the road and waits for the constables.

choices.text: Leave human law to humans

effects.log: He robs the crossing for a year, and then a better robber robs him. Roads are like that.

events.text: The robber the crossing caught has served his time, and come back. He stands in the middle of the five roads with a broom, and sweeps them every morning, all five, as far as he can see.

choices.text: Warm the road under his feet in winter

effects.log: The sweeper stops feeling the cold. He tells everyone the crossing is kind to him now. Nobody believes he was ever a robber.

choices.text: Leave him to his penance

effects.log: He sweeps them for the rest of his life. The crossroads is the cleanest in the land of men. When he dies they bury him at the edge of the east road.

events.text: Market day over you, every fifth day, and every fifth day the same weigher at the rice stall cheats with a thumb on the scale. You can feel the thumb from here. It is a small weight. It is the wrong weight.
variants: An old woman at the salt stall gives full weight and a pinch over, to every buyer, every fifth day, and has done for forty years. Her stall is the lightest thing on the market, and the warmest.
A magistrate's clerk is checking the market's weights, stall by stall. Half of the weights are short. The clerk is taking silver to forget.

choices.text: Tilt the scale back from below

effects.log: The weigher's thumb pushes and the earth pushes back. The rice comes out honest. The weigher looks at the thumb as if it belonged to somebody else.

choices.text: Make the stall shake when the thumb goes down

effects.log: The stall rattles every time. Customers start watching the scale. The weigher gives up the thumb within a month.

choices.text: Weigh the whole market instead

effects.log: A hundred stalls, and only three honest. You do not act. You remember, and grow heavy with it, like a stone.

events.text: Under the market you find a thing the market has forgotten: an old standard weight of bronze, buried when the town was young, the one all the other weights were cast to match.

choices.text: Push it up through the earth into the market square

effects.log: A child finds it after a rain, green and heavy. The elders know at once what it is. Every weight in the market is checked against it by autumn.

choices.text: Keep it, and learn its weight

effects.log: You hold it for a season. It is exactly the weight of a fair thing. You will not forget it.

choices.text: Leave it in the clay

effects.log: Some standards are better kept where nobody can shave them. You curl round it and sleep.

events.text: The bronze weight sits on a stone in the market now, under a little roof. The town swears oaths on it. A merchant, caught cheating, is made to stand beside it all market day in shame.

choices.text: Let the weight grow a little warm in his hand

effects.log: He touches it, expecting cold bronze, and finds it warm as a palm. He weeps in front of the whole market and pays back every buyer.

choices.text: Let the shame do the work

effects.log: The market watches. He goes home that night and never cheats again, and never comes to that market again either.

events.text: The magistrate's court sits on you now. Every case is a weight: a stolen ox, a broken promise, a death on the river. You feel each verdict as it falls, the true ones settling, the false ones lying crooked.
variants: A new magistrate has come, young and frightened, and sits on you like a sparrow on an ox. His first case is a widow's land. He does not know what to do.
The court's drum is beaten in the night: a petition nobody wants heard. You feel the drumbeats come down into the earth like a heart that is not yours.

choices.text: Make the false verdicts uncomfortable

effects.log: The magistrate's chair creaks after every bad judgement. He is not a stupid man. He starts to listen to the creaking.

choices.text: Feel the weight of the county, and endure it

effects.log: A county is heavy. You learn to carry it the way an ox learns a yoke, by leaning into it.

choices.text: Listen for the cases that never come to court

effects.log: They are the heaviest: the ones too poor to be heard. You find that you can hear them, faintly, from every village of the county.

events.text: The county's river is rising, and the dykes are old. You can feel the water pressing on the earth from the east, patient and very heavy.

choices.text: Hold the dyke from below through the flood

ok.log: For nine days the earth under the dyke does not give. The water goes round the county instead of through it.

fail.log: You hold most of it. One stretch gives, and three villages flood to the knee. You are bruised to the core.

choices.text: Open a path for the water to the low meadows

effects.log: The meadows drown. The villages do not. In the spring the meadows are the richest ground in the county.

choices.text: Shake the ground so the county wakes in time

effects.log: A small tremor at midnight. People run out of their houses, see the river, and run uphill. Nobody is lost.

events.text: {npc}, the young king who laid the palace over you, comes down alone to the cellar where the foundation stone sits. Kings, it seems, have heard the old stories too. {npc} sits on the stone and asks the earth for advice.
variants: The palace is asleep. {npc} has come down to the foundation stone again, as {npc} does on the worst nights, and is talking to it about a famine in the south.

choices.text: Answer, in a voice the stone remembers

effects.log: You speak. {npc} goes white, then very still, then listens to the end. The next morning the king cancels a war.

choices.text: Answer with warmth only

effects.log: The stone grows warm under the king. {npc} sits a long time, and goes up the stairs with straighter shoulders.

choices.text: Stay silent: a king must learn to decide

effects.log: {npc} waits all night and hears nothing, and goes up and decides alone, and decides well. You are prouder than if you had spoken.

events.text: The palace over you has become your temple, as the stories said it would. Courtiers bow to the floor of the throne hall without quite knowing why. A palace cook leaves a bowl of millet on the cellar step every night.

choices.text: Eat the millet

effects.log: Each bowl makes you a little more solid in the world of humans. The cook, finding the bowls empty, tells nobody and is never once ill.

choices.text: Listen to the whole palace at once

effects.log: Two thousand people above you. Plots, griefs, gossip, a newborn. You hold all of it like water in a jar.

choices.text: Settle the foundations a finger deeper

effects.log: The whole palace sinks a finger and is steadier for it. An earthquake in the spring cracks every building in the city but this one.

events.text: The pagoda over your heart is nine storeys high, and on windy nights it sways. You are the earth it stands on and the strength in its central pillar, and you feel every storey lean.
variants: Pilgrims are circling the pagoda, nine times each, a ring of feet around you that never stops from dawn to dusk. Their prayers come down the pillar like rain down a chain.
The pagoda's monks are repairing the fifth storey, and a novice has dropped a hammer. It falls nine storeys and lands, very gently, on its side.

choices.text: Lean back against the wind

effects.log: All night you lean. In the morning the pagoda stands straight and the monks find nothing amiss but a great deal of fallen tile.

choices.text: Let it sway: it was built to

effects.log: It sways and does not fall. The carpenter who built it knew what he was doing, and you are glad of him.

choices.text: Sing up the pillar to the bells at the top

effects.log: Nine bells ring at once, with no hand on them. The city wakes and says the pagoda has spoken.

events.text: Deep below the pagoda, deeper than you have ever gone, the old earth is shifting. A great quake is coming to the city, slow as a sigh and very large.

choices.text: Hold the city's ground still

ok.log: You hold it. The quake comes and goes and the city feels it as a shiver. The pagoda's bells ring once.

fail.log: You hold the centre and lose the edges. The outer wards crack and a bridge falls. The pagoda stands.

choices.text: Let it out slowly, over a year

effects.log: A year of small tremors instead of one great one. The city grumbles about the shaking and is never once destroyed.

choices.text: Wake the monks to ring the warning bells

effects.log: The bells ring all night. The city sleeps in the fields. The quake takes houses, and no people.

events.text: The roots of the old persimmon tree above have found you. They are thin and patient and very thirsty, and they have been feeling their way down through the clay toward your warmth for twenty years.
variants: The roots of a pine have reached the clay above you, and with them, faintly, the whole life of the pine: wind, birds, a child who climbs it every afternoon.

choices.text: Let them drink from you

effects.log: The persimmon fruits that autumn so heavily that a branch breaks. The whole place eats persimmons until they are sick of them.

choices.text: Lead them to the old spring instead

effects.log: You turn the roots, a finger a year, toward a seam of water. The tree lives another century.

choices.text: Learn how a root listens

effects.log: It listens with its whole length, the way you do. You had not known a tree could be a teacher.

events.text: An ant city has been built against your flank: ten thousand rooms, a queen, a war with the red ants of the next furrow. It is a whole kingdom, and it has no idea it is living on a dragon.

choices.text: Watch how the ants keep their roads

effects.log: Every road shared, every load carried by whoever is nearest. The human roads above you could learn from it.

choices.text: End the war: warm the furrow between them

effects.log: The ground between the two cities grows too warm to cross. The war stops for want of a battlefield.

choices.text: Let the kingdom be

effects.log: Kingdoms come and go above you and beside you. This one lasts eleven summers, which for ants is a reign of note.

events.text: Somebody has buried a jar of coins a forearm above your back: a widow's savings, hidden from a son who spends faster than he earns. Tonight a spade is coming down toward it, in the wrong hands.

choices.text: Sink the jar a little deeper

effects.log: The spade finds clay, and more clay, and a stone. The digger gives up before dawn. The widow never knows how close it was.

choices.text: Turn the spade aside onto an old bone

effects.log: The digger strikes a bone, decides the place is a grave, and runs.

choices.text: Leave human silver to humans

effects.log: The jar comes up. Somewhere above you there is a quarrel that lasts years. You remember the weight of the jar, and the lightness after.

events.text: The eighteen dead days before the turn of the season, when the old people say no one should dig, and someone is digging anyway: a new privy, by the sound of it, right above your head.
variants: The dead days again, the hinge between two seasons, and the whole earth above you lies still and heavy as a held breath. Even the moles keep to their tunnels.
The eighteen days before summer: the spring hands itself over through you, slow and heavy, and the humans above put off their building until it is done.
The dead days before winter. A carpenter above you is arguing with an old woman about whether a post may go in the ground now. The old woman is winning.

choices.text: Shake the spade out of their hands

effects.log: The digger drops the spade, hears the old people's warnings in their head all at once, and goes to dig somewhere else after the season turns.

choices.text: Bear it: they need the privy

effects.log: A hole in the earth during the dead days is a sore spot, like a pulled tooth. You bear it. You are not as fragile as the old people think.

choices.text: Rest in the dead days, as the season wants

effects.log: You let the year turn through you, eighteen days of slow, heavy changing. The privy is the least of it.

events.text: The kitchen god of the house above has noticed you. It sits in the hearth at night, small and soot-black, and talks down through the floor about the family: who eats too much, who is in love, who stole the honey.

choices.text: Talk back

effects.log: You have never talked to anyone before. You find you have opinions about the honey.

choices.text: Ask it how to keep a house

effects.log: It knows a great deal about keeping a house, mostly about watching. It is a good teacher and very rude.

choices.text: Warm its hearth from below in winter

effects.log: The house's fire never quite goes out that winter. The kitchen god is embarrassingly grateful.

events.text: An old woman of the place above has been buried at the edge of the ground you hold, in good clay, facing south. Her family weeps above for three days. Her bones are cold.

choices.text: Warm the clay around her

effects.log: Her grave is the only one in the hills where the snow melts first each spring. Her family says she always hated the cold.

choices.text: Keep the water from her grave

effects.log: No water reaches her. Her grave stays dry for a hundred years, which is the best thing the earth can give.

choices.text: Let the earth do what earth does

effects.log: She goes back into the clay the slow way, and becomes, in time, a little of you. You find you know a few of her songs.

events.text: A geomancer is walking the ground above you with a compass of nine rings, looking for the dragon vein that makes a site lucky. The needle is spinning. It has found you, and does not know what to do about it.
variants: Two geomancers are arguing over the ground above you, each with a compass, each sure the dragon vein runs a different way. Both are wrong, and one of them is standing on your head.

choices.text: Show the needle the true line

effects.log: The needle settles on your spine. The geomancer goes white, bows to the empty ground, and charges the client double.

choices.text: Make the needle point somewhere harmless

effects.log: The geomancer chooses a hill a li away, which is a perfectly good hill. You keep your secret.

choices.text: Let the needle spin

effects.log: It spins all afternoon. The geomancer writes in a notebook that the site is "too lucky", which is a new category.

events.text: Deep in the clay, near your heart, you find something hard and round: an old temple bell, buried in a war long before the town above was built. It still remembers how to ring.

choices.text: Ring it once, from below

effects.log: The whole town hears a bell where there is no bell. The monks dig for a year and find it, and hang it again.

choices.text: Keep it, and listen to it remember

effects.log: It remembers its last morning: a war, a fire, monks running. You hold it until it is quiet.

choices.text: Sink it deeper, where no war will find it

effects.log: Some things should stay buried. You curl round it and sink.

events.text: The mountain god of the hills to the north has come down to the edge of your ground to argue about the boundary. It is an old god, with a tiger at its side, and very sure the river is the line.

choices.text: Agree the river is the line

effects.log: It is not quite, but it is close enough, and a mountain god as a friend is worth a strip of riverbank.

choices.text: Hold your ground

ok.log: The ground holds. The mountain god nods, as one holder of land to another, and goes back up into the pines.

fail.log: The tiger leans on the bank and the bank slides. You keep most of it. The god keeps a slice and a smile.

choices.text: Ask the mountain god what the hills need

effects.log: Rain, mostly, and fewer woodcutters. You can help with one of those. The boundary is forgotten.

events.text: Drought. The rulers above you have gone out to the altar in hemp robes to pray for rain, and the people stand in the dust and watch the sky. Nobody is watching the ground.

choices.text: Send water up through every well at once

effects.log: Every well in the place rises a hand's breadth overnight. It is not rain, but it is enough to wait for rain.

choices.text: Call to the dragons of the rain

effects.log: You are earth, not water, but the rain dragons are cousins. Three days later a long grey cloud comes from the east, grumbling.

choices.text: Hold the moisture in the earth and wait

effects.log: You keep the damp in the deep soil. When the rain comes at last, the seeds that were in your keeping come up first.

events.text: A great tomb is being raised on the hill beside your ground for a ruler not yet dead. Ten thousand labourers carry earth on their backs, and you feel every one of them, tired to the bone.

choices.text: Make the earth lighter to carry

effects.log: The baskets weigh less than baskets should. The labourers finish a year early and go home.

choices.text: Make the hill refuse the tomb

effects.log: The trenches flood, the walls slide. The ruler's geomancers declare the hill unlucky, and the labourers are sent home.

choices.text: Let the work go on, and remember the labourers

effects.log: You know every name by the end of it. When the ruler is buried there at last, it is their names you think of.

events.text: Very deep, under all of it, you find the bones of an older yellow dragon: one that held this ground before the first house was built, and went back into the earth when its time came. The bones are still warm.

choices.text: Lie beside them for a season

effects.log: Something passes from the old bones to you: not strength, but the shape of a long patience. You come up older.

choices.text: Ask the bones what came before

effects.log: In the warmth there is a memory: a plain with no houses, and a dragon waiting for the first one.

choices.text: Leave them their rest

effects.log: You go back up through the clay and leave the old one sleeping. Someday you will lie here too.

events.text: Spring ploughing above you: the iron coming down through the topsoil, the oxen leaning, the seed going in. You can feel the whole year beginning in a single furrow.
variants: Harvest above you: the weight of the stooks, the sound of sickles, the children gleaning. The earth is tired and pleased, like a mother after a feast.
First snow on the ground above you. Everything goes quiet. The humans stay in, the animals sleep, and the earth and you are alone together for a while.
Summer weeding above you: hoes in the rows, children carrying water, an old man asleep under a tree at noon. The earth is warm all the way down to you.
Autumn wind over the ground you hold, and the first frost in the furrows. The humans above are bringing everything in, as if the earth might change its mind.

choices.text: Wake the soil under the seed

effects.log: The seeds over your back come up three days before anyone else's. The farmer is smug about it all summer.

choices.text: Turn with the year

effects.log: Spring, summer, the dead days, autumn, the dead days, winter, the dead days. You let it all go through you once, slowly.

choices.text: Sleep through the ploughing

effects.log: It is like being scratched. You sleep through the whole of it and wake to a field of green.

events.text: A child above you has dug a hole in the yard to see what is at the bottom of the world. It is a very determined child and a very deep hole, and it is getting close.

choices.text: Let the child find one warm stone

effects.log: The child brings up a stone as warm as a hand and keeps it forever. The family thinks the child has a fever, and then decides not to worry.

choices.text: Fill the hole with water so the child stops

effects.log: The hole becomes a puddle, and the puddle becomes a pond for frogs, which the child likes better.

choices.text: Make the clay too hard to dig

effects.log: The spade bounces. The child concludes that the bottom of the world is very hard, and becomes, in time, a stonemason.

events.text: An army is marching over your ground: heavy, fast, and too many, the kind of weight you have learned means a battle somewhere ahead. The place above you is in its road.

choices.text: Make the road soft, so the army slows

effects.log: Wheels sink, horses stumble. The army takes four days to cross land it should have crossed in one, and the place above you has time to bar its gates.

choices.text: Shake the ground under the vanguard

ok.log: The vanguard's horses bolt. The general takes it for an omen and turns the army aside.

fail.log: The army is too heavy to frighten. It crosses anyway, and you are bruised and very tired.

choices.text: Let it pass: armies come and go

effects.log: It passes. You hold the place above you steady under the boots, and it stands when the army has gone.

events.text: Tomb-robbers are tunnelling through the clay toward the old graves at the edge of your ground. They are clever, and quiet, and they have a lantern that smells of bad oil.

choices.text: Close the tunnel on them, gently

ok.log: The tunnel narrows until they cannot go on. They back out, shaking, and swear off graves for good.

fail.log: They are quicker than the clay. They get one jar out before you close the tunnel, and you strain something deep.

choices.text: Breathe on their lantern

effects.log: It goes out. In the dark, under the earth, with something breathing, they find that they have urgent business elsewhere.

choices.text: Let the dead keep their own graves

effects.log: The robbers find the graves, and in them nothing but clay. The dead took their things with them long ago.

events.text: Dawn on the high ridge. You sing, as you have sung every dawn, and wait. The valley below fills with light. No voice answers yet.
variants: Rain on the high ridge, and you sing into it anyway. The song comes back to you off the wet rocks, louder than you sent it, and for a moment you think it is an answer.
A paulownia on the ridge has come into flower. You sit in it and sing the flowers open, one by one.

choices.text: Sing again, softer

effects.log: A softer song carries further. Far off, three ridges away, something might be listening. You cannot tell.

choices.text: Sing to the humans in the valley instead

effects.log: A shepherd stops on the path and listens with his mouth open. He will tell the story badly for the rest of his life.

choices.text: Stop singing and listen

effects.log: The wind, the pines, a stream. A long time of nothing. Then, very faint, a note that is not an echo.

events.text: The two of you fly together now, and the first nest has to be built: a nest of paulownia twigs, bamboo seed and nothing that was ever taken from anyone.
variants: A storm has torn half the nest away, and the two of you rebuild it in the rain, twig by twig, without a single argument.
Humans in the valley have planted a line of paulownia saplings along the ridge path. They are hoping you will nest there. One of the saplings is very good.

choices.text: Gather only fallen twigs

effects.log: It takes a whole season to find enough. The nest is small and perfect.

choices.text: Ask a grove for its oldest branch

effects.log: The grove lets one go in a storm, as if it had been waiting. It is the heart of the nest.

choices.text: Let your mate choose where

effects.log: Your mate chooses a cliff you would never have chosen. It is better than any you would have chosen.

events.text: The bamboo of the far valley is flowering, as it does once in sixty years, and its seed is the only food a phoenix truly wants. Every bird of the mountains is going to the valley, and so are the rats.

choices.text: Go and eat your fill

effects.log: A month of bamboo seed. You come back heavier and brighter, and your song has a new note in it.

choices.text: Gather seed for the lean years

effects.log: You carry seed to a dry cave, mouthful by mouthful. In the lean years after, you and the birds you share it with are the only fat things in the hills.

choices.text: Keep the rats from stripping the valley

effects.log: You stand guard over the flowering bamboo. The valley's seed lasts long enough for the bamboo to grow again.

events.text: A bird-catcher from the valley has climbed the ridge with a net of silk and a cage of gilded bamboo. Somebody rich below has promised gold for a bird that sings like a dawn.

choices.text: Sing so the net forgets how to close

effects.log: The silk tangles on nothing, three times. The bird-catcher goes home with an empty cage and a song stuck in their head for the rest of their life.

choices.text: Fly at the net and tear it

ok.log: The net goes to pieces in the wind like a spider's web. The bird-catcher runs.

fail.log: The silk catches a wing. You tear free with a lost feather and a sore shoulder.

choices.text: Fly to another ridge for a season

effects.log: You sing somewhere else until the bird-catcher gives up. The old ridge is still yours when you come back.

events.text: The hardest winter of your years on the pass. Snow to the shoulder, the deer gone down to the valleys, and the villagers' cattle in their byres, warm and close and very tempting.

choices.text: Go down to the valleys after the deer

effects.log: A long hunt in deep snow, and a thin winter. You keep your word to the villages without ever having given it.

choices.text: Take one ox from the richest byre

effects.log: The richest farmer loses an ox and the village laughs at him behind its hands. Nobody else loses anything all winter.

choices.text: Sleep in a cave and wait it out

effects.log: You wake thin and stiff in a world of melting snow, and very hungry, and alive.

events.text: Another tiger has come over the far ridge: young, scarred and hungry for a pass of its own. Its scent is on your rocks this morning, very deliberately.

choices.text: Meet it at the top of the pass

ok.log: A short, terrible fight in the snow. It goes back over the ridge, and the pass is yours.

fail.log: It is stronger than you guessed. You keep the pass with a torn ear and a limp that lasts the winter.

choices.text: Show it the valley over the next ridge, which is empty

effects.log: It goes. Two tigers on two passes, and neither hungry. The villages are very nervous about it for a generation.

choices.text: Mark your rocks again, higher

effects.log: You mark them higher than any tiger could reach. The young one reads it and thinks better of it.

events.text: The dry year: every spring in the district has failed but yours, and the villages are walking for a day to fill their jars at it. Some of them are pushing to the front.

choices.text: Butt the ones who push

effects.log: Gently, but every time. By the end of the week the line is the most orderly thing in the district.

choices.text: Eat only the bitter leaf, so the spring stays clean

effects.log: You keep the spring as clean as the first day. It holds out to the end of the dry year, and so do the villages.

choices.text: Go and find the springs that failed

effects.log: Two of them are only choked with leaves. You clear them, and the line at your spring halves.

events.text: The red sand of the cave shifts around the egg. Something is walking in the cave mouth: a fox, sniffing, curious, very hungry.

choices.text: Glow, once, very red

effects.log: The fox sees a coal in the sand where no fire is, and goes away fast.

choices.text: Stay cold and dull as a stone

effects.log: The fox noses the egg, decides it is a stone, and leaves.

events.text: Travellers on the mountain road at dusk: a salt-trader with a mule, a monk, a family moving house. They walk close together and do not look at the trees, because they know the mountain has a tiger.
variants: Snow on the high road, and someone is stuck in it: a mail-runner with a frozen foot, very afraid of the dark, more afraid of what is in it.
A hunter has set a trap on your mountain, cleverly, on the path a young deer takes to the stream.

choices.text: Walk beside them in the trees, unseen, to the top

effects.log: They reach the top in the dark and never know they were guarded. A wolf pack that was following turns back at your scent.

choices.text: Let them see you once, and pass

effects.log: You cross the path in front of them, slowly, and are gone. The story of the tiger who let them pass is told at their hearths for years.

choices.text: Leave them to the road

effects.log: They are nervous, and safe. You lie on a rock in the last sun, and are a tiger.

events.text: Four of you in the den, blind and warm. One of your brothers keeps climbing on your head. Outside, very far off, something is calling: the mother of the den, coming back.
events.arc: The Den in the First Snow

choices.text: Crawl toward the sound

effects.log: You are first to her. She licks you so hard you fall over.

choices.text: Push your brother off your head

effects.log: He falls. He climbs back. This will be your life, you understand.

events.text: Two neighbours have brought a quarrel to your spring: a fence moved in the night, a strip of field lost. Both swear it was the other. One of them is lying, and is very good at it.
variants: A child has brought a quarrel to your spring: a lost marble, an older cousin, a very clear sense of justice. The cousin is hiding behind the headman's wall.
The headman of the village has a quarrel with the whole village about a tax, and has brought it to your spring, which is brave of him, since he is wrong.

choices.text: Butt the liar, gently

effects.log: Your horn finds the liar as a needle finds north. The fence goes back the next morning. The village nods: it always works.

choices.text: Wait until the liar admits it

effects.log: You stand and look at them both, all afternoon. Near sunset the liar cannot bear it, and confesses.

choices.text: Butt the fence instead

effects.log: You knock it flat. The two of them have to rebuild it together, and argue, and in the end agree where it goes.

events.text: The spring where you were born is very cold and very clear. A fox comes down to drink and looks at you sideways, with a lie already in its mouth.

choices.text: Lower your horn-bud at it

effects.log: The fox decides not to lie today. It drinks and goes.

choices.text: Watch it drink, and learn what a lie looks like

effects.log: It looks like a fox drinking. That is the first thing you learn about lies.

events.text: The fire jar is cold except for you. The night is the coldest of the year, and the family is asleep around the jar, close, because you are all the warmth they have.

choices.text: Burn as bright as you dare

effects.log: You burn until morning. The family wakes warm and does not know why the jar has not gone out.

choices.text: Burn low and last

effects.log: You keep a small red heart all night. In the morning the grandmother blows on you, and you leap up, and she laughs.

events.text: Your maker's hand is warm and dry and shakes a little. Someone is knocking at the door: soldiers, looking for iron for the war.

choices.text: Lie still as rice

effects.log: The soldiers look at a few grains of rice in an old palm and go away.

choices.text: Taste the needle in the maker's sleeve

effects.log: It is your first iron. It goes down like a spark. The soldiers do not notice a needle missing.

events.text: A child in a village at the edge of your range has drawn you on a wall, in charcoal: huge, ridiculous and recognisable. The child's grandmother says her own grandmother saw you once, in this same spot.
variants: Someone in the valley has carved your likeness over a village gate. It is a good likeness. They have given you kind eyes, which you are not sure you deserve.
Three generations of one family have left a bowl of clean water at the same stone for you, every spring. This spring the bowl is held out by someone very small.

choices.text: Show yourself to the child, once

effects.log: The child does not scream. The child waves. You find that you have no idea what to do, and go away very slowly.

choices.text: Leave something by the drawing

effects.log: A feather, a shed scale, a stone warm from your body. The family keeps it for nine generations.

choices.text: Go on your way

effects.log: The drawing stays on the wall for a hundred years. The village paints over it at last, and the child, old now, draws you again.

events.text: The grandchildren of hunters who once came for you are hunters too, with better bows and the old stories. Five of them are in your range this autumn, following the signs very carefully.
variants: Torches in your range at night: hunters, young and loud, with a great-grandfather's map that marks your den with a red circle.
A hunting party has come into your range with dogs, horns and a banner. Someone important wants your hide on a wall, and has paid others to fetch it.
Two hunters are sitting by a fire at the edge of your range, arguing about whether you are real. One of them has a very good bow.

choices.text: Meet them where you choose

ok.log: You come out of the rain in front of them and stand there. They do not draw. They go home, and the stories change.

fail.log: One of them is very good. You take an arrow before they flee, and carry it in you for a season.

choices.text: Lead them in circles until winter

effects.log: They walk your range for two months and find your tracks everywhere and you nowhere. They go home with a new respect for the old stories.

choices.text: Let them find an old shed skin and go home proud

effects.log: They carry it home like a prize. It is a prize, of a kind. Nobody comes the next autumn.

events.text: You have lived through so many winters that you can tell this one's shape by the first frost: a hard one, short, with an early thaw. The young things of your range do not know it yet.
variants: The forest of your range has turned over: every tree in it has grown, fallen and been replaced since you first came. You are older than the whole forest.
A comet in the sky, the second time you have seen it. The first time you were small and afraid of it. This time you watch it all night.
A wet year, the wettest you remember, and you remember a great many. Streams where there were none, moss on everything, and the young things of your range drowning in plenty.
Spring comes late to your range this year, and all at once: one morning snow, the next morning flowers, as if the year had overslept and was trying to hide it.

choices.text: Sleep through the hard part

effects.log: You sleep for six weeks and wake to the thaw, rested and very hungry.

choices.text: Keep watch over the young things of your range

effects.log: You lie by the frozen stream where the deer come, and nothing hunts there that winter.

choices.text: Spend the winter remembering

effects.log: The winters of your life, one after another, back to the first. Each one teaches you something you missed the first time.

events.text: A young one of your kind has wandered into your range, half-starved and very proud, and is pretending not to be afraid of you.
events.arc: A Young One of Your Kind

choices.text: Show it where the food is

effects.log: It eats for a week without once looking grateful. It stays a year, and leaves knowing a great deal more than it came with.

choices.text: Test it, so it knows how far it has to go

ok.log: It loses, as it should, and gets up, and tries again the next day. You like it.

fail.log: It is stronger than you guessed. You win in the end, with a torn ear, and it goes off very pleased with itself.

choices.text: Leave it to find its own way

effects.log: It finds its own way, slowly, and comes back a hundred years later to thank you for nothing, which is the right thanks.
